content.comment_body: We are experiencing a similar problem: when attempting to access the [product_name] web server, it only responds with '192.168.0.3/Multilingual_readMe_OSS.html - [company_name] Third Party Disclosure Agreement.' Our hardware is [article_no] [product_name] with firmware [version_no]. The device IP is 192.168.0.3 on a LAN connected solely to a PC. The PC uses [product_name] v8.4 and Microsoft Edge Version 125.0.2535.67, with IP 192.168.0.55. The device is programmed and operating normally, and the clock has been updated. Access Control for Web Server Access (HTTP) and Web User are both enabled. We have tried saving, importing, and managing certificate settings within [product_name], as well as restarting both hardware and software multiple times.
Please initiate a support request for troubleshooting.
I am facing the same problem: unable to access the web server and seeing the same message.

Hello, if the only content visible is 'Multilingual_readMe_OSS.html - [company_name] Third Party Disclosure Agreement' on the [product_name] web server, it means the web server is not enabled. Only OSS information will display until the web server feature is properly activated. To enable the web server and password, click 'Apply.' Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are reporting difficulties accessing the intended web interface for their [product_name] device, receiving only a [company_name] Third Party Disclosure Agreement page. Despite checking settings, restarting devices, and importing security certificates, the web server remains inaccessible. Support clarified that the issue is likely related to the web server feature not being fully enabled, emphasizing potential usability or discoverability challenges in the product's setup interface.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect easy and direct access to the [product_name] web server interface after following standard configuration steps. They anticipate that managing security certificates, network settings, and user access options should suffice for connectivity, without hidden or undocumented activation requirements.
